omg.si.discrete_flow_matching_uniform module#

class omg.si.discrete_flow_matching_uniform.DiscreteFlowMatchingUniform(noise: float = 0.0)[source]#

Bases: StochasticInterpolantSpecies

Class for discrete flow matching (DFM) between categorical distributions based on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04997.

This class is currently designed for uniform base distributions p_0 for the points x_0.

Parameters:

noise (float) – Parameter scaling the noise that should be added during integration.

Raises:

ValueError – If the number of integration steps is less than or equal to 0 or the noise is less than 0.

__init__(noise: float = 0.0) → None[source]#

Construct DiscreteFlowMatchingMask class.

integrate(model_function: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], tuple[Tensor, Tensor]], x_t: Tensor, time: Tensor, time_step: Tensor, batch_indices: Tensor) → Tensor[source]#

Integrate the current positions x_t at the given time for the given time step based on the probability distributions over the species.

In contrast to the other stochastic interpolants in this module, the model prediction is not the velocity fields b and denoisers eta. Instead, only one model prediction is required. The second model prediction is ignored in this class.

Given that x_0 is of shape (sum(n_atoms),) containing the species of every atom in the batch, the model prediction returns a tensor of shape (sum(n_atoms), MAX_ATOM_NUM) containing the probability distribution over the species (excluding the mask with token 0) of every atom in the batch.

Following https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04997, we construct a rate matrix R by R(i,j|x_1) = ReLU((dp(j|x_1)/dt) - (dp(x_t|x_1)) / (S * p(x_t|x_1)), and add noise via “detailed balance” rate matrices R_db (see appendix) R_db(i,j|x_1) = eta * delta(i,x_1) + eta * delta(j, x_1) * (St + 1 - t) / (1 - t). We adapt the code in Listing 8 in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04997.

In addition, we discretize time instead of using a continuous time Markov process.

TODO: I think we should implement a continuous-time Markov process in the future.

TODO: We should introduce an abstract class based on the abstract functions in Listing 8. Then this should work for arbitrary base distributions.

Parameters:

  • model_function (Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]) – Model function returning the probability distributions over the species given the current times t and positions x_t.

  • x_t (torch.Tensor) – Current positions.

  • time (torch.Tensor) – Initial time (0-dimensional torch tensor).

  • time_step (torch.Tensor) – Time step (0-dimensional torch tensor).

  • batch_indices (torch.Tensor) – Tensor containing the configuration index for every atom in the batch.

interpolate(t: Tensor, x_0: Tensor, x_1: Tensor, batch_indices: Tensor) → tuple[Tensor, Tensor][source]#

Interpolate between points x_0 and x_1 from two distributions p_0 and p_1 at times t using discrete flow matching.

The base points x_0 are expected to be entirely in the masked state.

Parameters:

  • t (torch.Tensor) – Times in [0,1].

  • x_0 (torch.Tensor) – Points from p_0.

  • x_1 (torch.Tensor) – Points from p_1.

  • batch_indices (torch.Tensor) – Tensor containing the configuration index for every atom in the batch.

Returns:

Interpolated points x_t, random variables z used for interpolation.

Return type:

tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]

loss(model_function: Callable[[Tensor], tuple[Tensor, Tensor]], t: Tensor, x_0: Tensor, x_1: Tensor, x_t: Tensor, z: Tensor, batch_indices: Tensor) → Dict[str, Tensor][source]#

Compute the cross-entropy loss for the discrete flow matching between points x_0 and x_1 from two distributions p_0 and p_1 at times t based on the model prediction for the probability distributions over the species.

In contrast to the other stochastic interpolants in this module, the model prediction is not the velocity fields b and denoisers eta. Instead, only one model prediction is required. The second model prediction is ignored in this class.

This class returns a single loss with the key ‘loss’.

Given that x_0 is of shape (sum(n_atoms),) containing the species of every atom in the batch, the model prediction returns a tensor of shape (sum(n_atoms), MAX_ATOM_NUM) containing the probability distribution over the species (excluding the mask with token 0) of every atom in the batch.

Parameters:

  • model_function (Callable[[torch.Tensor], tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]) – Model function returning the velocity fields b and the denoisers eta given the current positions x_t.

  • t (torch.Tensor) – Times in [0,1].

  • x_0 (torch.Tensor) – Points from p_0.

  • x_1 (torch.Tensor) – Points from p_1.

  • x_t – Stochastically interpolated points x_t:

  • z (torch.Tensor) – Random variable z that was used for the stochastic interpolation to get the model prediction.

  • batch_indices (torch.Tensor) – Tensor containing the configuration index for every atom in the batch.

Returns:

Cross-entropy loss.

Return type:

Dict[str, torch.Tensor]
